Assessment of Acid-Base Balance
It is an understatement to say that assessment of acid-base
disturbances is diﬃ  cult. Th is diﬃ  culty arises because of the
body’s attempt to self-correct changes in pH. Th ese compensa-
tory responses confuse the clinical situation, making origin of 
the disturbance diﬃ  cult to assess. Many times, assessment of 
acid-base balance requires more than simply examining labora-
tory values—it needs to be put into the context of the patient’s

values elicits only the current state of blood pH. Th is, of course,
